papers.title: One Polynomial Field for Every Euler Step and the Flow: Polynomial Dynamics for P and PSPACE
papers.abstract: We construct, for each deterministic Turing machine that halts on all inputs, one polynomial vector field with rational coefficients that performs the same logical computation at unit Euler step, at every smaller or variable step in $(0,1]$ with divergent sum, and along the flow. This unifies discrete-time and continuous-time computation by polynomial dynamics, which earlier characterizations treated separately. For a machine making $T$ transitions in space $H$, a logical scale $h=2^{-s}$ with $s=O(H)$ suffices, with physical time $O(s(T+s))$, drift disturbances up to $h^{2K}$ for a fixed exponent $K$, and $2Ks+3$ fractional bits at unit step. On a fixed compact domain, polynomial time and robust eventual decision characterize P and PSPACE, respectively, with polynomial scale thresholds and no supplied stabilization horizon in the space case. Without sign, floor or conditional primitives, margin amplification at bounded speed, overlapping polynomial gates and interval-product estimates give the common realization, from which we derive shared logical traces, fixed-field PSPACE-complete prediction and a robust safety family with polynomial certificates common to all Euler steps and the flow.

papers.title: Nonlinear Nonlocal Diffusion Equations for the Analysis of Coordination
papers.abstract: Coordination games with explicit spatial or relational structure are of interest to economists, ecologists, sociologists, and others studying emergent global properties in collective behavior. When assemblies of individuals seek to coordinate action with one another through myopic best response or other replicator dynamics, the resulting dynamical system can exhibit many rich behaviors. Here we seek to understand these coordination dynamics in the non-atomic setting by use of a nonlinear, nonlocal diffusion equation framework. For this class of nonlocal equations, we prove existence and uniqueness for the initial value problem in the free boundary case and, with certain conditions on the underlying game theory, we go further and prove a maximum principle, weak regularity results, and a characterization of asymptotic behavior. Additionally, with the help of several numerical results, we present several modeling results, characterizing stationary solutions both rigorously and through numerical experiments.

papers.title: Learning Kolmogorov Backward Operators for Spectral Analysis and Forecasting: A Data-Driven Variational Galerkin Framework
papers.abstract: For a time-homogeneous Markov process, the fixed-lag solution operator \( (T_\tau f)(x)=\mathbb E[f(X_{t+\tau})\mid X_t=x] \) of the Kolmogorov backward equation evolves observables linearly and deterministically, even when the dynamics are stochastic. We approximate this operator using a two-stage method where we first approximate this operator directly from data, without knowledge of the governing equation (e.g., Fourier Neural Operator), and then compress the Galerkin projection onto a finite-dimensional observable space that is fixed in advance or selected variationally. The error analysis traces the learning error of the estimator, the sampling error of the Galerkin inner products, and the invariance and reconstruction properties of the observable space to the computed spectra and forecasts. The sampling error enters only through a multiplicative factor. Near an isolated spectral cluster, the invariance defect of a subspace controls its distance from the target invariant subspace. The forecast error is controlled by the one-step error of the reduced model and the projection error of the observable; when the measure is invariant and the reduced model preserves constants and is stable on mean-zero observables, the bound is uniform in the horizon. For deterministic dynamics, a learning rate for Fourier neural operators (FNOs) gives one explicit bound for the learning error. Numerical experiments illustrate spectral approximation and forecasting, including long-rollout stability and a comparison with extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) when fewer transition pairs than basis functions are observed.

papers.title: Unified transform method for nonautonomous linear evolution equations: rigorous analysis and qualitative theory
papers.abstract: Established herein is the rigorous extension of the celebrated Fokas unified transform method for linear evolution PDE with time-dependent coefficients. As illustrative examples, considered below and rigorously analysed in detail are non-homogeneous initial-boundary-value problems, formulated on the half-line, for the heat equation and the modified heat (also widely known as Barenblatt's pseudo-parabolic) equation with reaction terms and temporally varying coefficients. Solution formulae are derived formally via suitable implementation of the UTM, and rigorously verified a posteriori, in the classical sense. The latter task relies on complex-analytic tools and careful interpretation of the obtained integral representations. The explicit solutions established here are then used for investigating qualitative properties. These include regularity, boundary behavior near the axes of the domain as well as long-range and eventual periodicity asymptotics. Notably, smoothness of the solution up to the boundaries depends on compatibility conditions between initial, boundary and forcing data, into which interjected now are initial values of the coefficients. Further results pertaining to solution uniqueness, analyticity and controllability of the addressed problems are thence deduced in light of the preceding qualitative theory.

papers.title: A dynamical approach to Frobenius splitting
papers.abstract: A dynamical system can be associated to the process of decomposing iterated Frobenius pushforwards of modules into indecomposable direct summands. Via this connection, we apply the theory of Markov chains to study asymptotic counts of multiplicities of indecomposable summands in the iterated Frobenius pushforwards of the given module, as the number of iterations grows. Our results recover and extend the existing results on the existence of the (generalized) F-signature due to Hashimoto--Symonds, Hashimoto--Kobayashi, Smith--Van den Bergh, Tucker, and Yao. We also develop further the theory of F-contributors, the modules for which the multiplicity grows at the maximal possible rate. As a key algebraic input, we define and develop strongly F-regular modules, extending Hochster--Huneke's notion of strongly F-regular rings. We use strongly F-regular modules to prove convergence of the relevant sequences and algebraically characterize F-contributors, when the underlying ring admits a module-finite strongly F-regular extension or has dimension at most two.

papers.title: Existence and spectral instability of steady rolls in the Nikolaevskiy equation: a computer-assisted study
papers.abstract: The Nikolaevskiy equation is a model of short-wave pattern formation coupled to a neutral long-wave mode, and it is believed that all of its spatially periodic steady states are unstable. Existing results are formal, numerical, or restricted to a small neighbourhood of onset. We give computer-assisted proofs of three results. First, for every wavenumber q in [0.9, 1.1] and every control parameter r between the onset value (1-q^2)^2 and 4, the equation has a nontrivial, real-analytic, odd steady roll; these rolls form a single continuous two-parameter family that bifurcates from the trivial state at onset, with an explicit amplitude bound proportional to the square root of the distance to onset. Second, every roll of this family with r in [0.25, 4] is spectrally unstable on the real line: its linearisation has a Bloch eigenvalue with real part at least 6.7e-4, and at least 0.13 for r >= 0.575. Third, at nine sample points we enclose, at a small Bloch number, the eigenvalue numerically identified with the long-wave (Matthews-Cox) branch; its real part is positive at seven points and negative at two, while strongly unstable eigenvalues exist at all nine. The proofs combine a parametrised Newton-Kantorovich theorem, a desingularisation near onset, Taylor-model bounds on parameter boxes, and a Weyl-sequence argument for the Bloch spectrum; all estimates are evaluated in rigorous interval arithmetic.

papers.title: Nonlinear springs with orbits in radicals: a solvability criterion
papers.abstract: An odd polynomial oscillator has a periodic orbit given by a quadrature. When the zeros of the energy polynomial are all simple or all of even multiplicity, that quadrature is elementary exactly when the polynomial is a perfect square, and the time is a sum of inverse tangents. Recovering the displacement inverts that relation, algebraic when their coefficients are commensurate, making a closed form a Galois question. This paper identifies the group as the monodromy group of a rational map, computes its branch data from the parameters, and shows the branch value at the phase-angle singularity never vanishes, so every decomposition pairs the amplitudes reciprocally. In the commensurate family with distinct real factors, the orbit is radical exactly when the primitive inversion degree is at most four, or when reciprocal pairs leave a reduced spring of that degree. Radical orbits occur at the fifth, ninth, thirteenth and seventeenth force orders, the last only for reciprocal members, an expression recorded for each. The multiplicity hypothesis cannot be dropped. Factoring the energy polynomial into square and squarefree parts turns the quadrature into a differential of the third kind on a hyperelliptic curve, where elementarity is a torsion condition on the divisor of its poles with a vanishing holomorphic remainder. The first nonsquare elementary member appears at the ninth force order, and the power pullback inverts in closed form at every such order, giving a radical orbit for a confining spring of arbitrarily high degree with a sufficient condition for positive coefficients.

papers.title: Symmetry-resolved periods in a cyclic-dominance automaton: separating intrinsic from lattice-induced periodicity
papers.abstract: Periodic attractors of spatially extended systems possess not one period but a hierarchy of periods, one for each level of observation and symmetry quotient, and this hierarchy separates how a pattern evolves from how it fits the finite domain. For a synchronous threshold model of cyclic dominance on an $L\times L$ torus, equivalent to the three-color cyclic cellular automaton of Fisch, Gravner and Griffeath, we measure for every attractor a \emph{tuple} of periods: that of the populations ($\Tpop$), of the full configuration ($\Tst$), and of the configuration up to color rotations ($\Tcol$), lattice symmetries ($\Tgeo$) and the full space--color group ($\TG$). Equivariance implies exact divisibility relations and the factorization $\Tst=\TG\,m$, where $m$ counts the applications of the symmetry $h$ that maps the configuration onto itself after $\TG$ steps: $\TG$ and the type of $h$ belong to the pattern, $m$ to the lattice, and the attractors are relative periodic orbits whose full period emerges from the interaction between the intrinsic dynamics and the lattice symmetries. A family of attractors built around a pair of counter-rotating spirals, with $\Tpop=24$ and $\TG=8$, persists from $L=9$ to $L=40$ while $\Tst$ takes values from 24 to 960, given in every case by the order of $h$; on a rectangular $9\times12$ torus it takes the value 48, absent from all square tori. With more than $4.5\times10^5$ runs at each of $L=8$ and $L=9$ we estimate the basins of attraction: fixed points take 95--97\% of the configuration space, and no single period is enough to tell the oscillating attractors apart. The same analysis locates local diversity: it is balanced whenever the cycle has a color symmetry and, on large lattices, it is concentrated at the spiral cores.

papers.title: Strong stable sets and asymptotic fineness
papers.abstract: We investigate the strong stable sets of the geodesic flow on hyperbolic surfaces and their relation to the injectivity radius. We prove that the strong stable set of a vector does not coincide with its stable horocycle if and only if the injectivity radius along the associated geodesic ray is not bounded away from zero and the ray does not diverge through a cusp. In that case, the strong stable set is an uncountable union of stable horocycles. In previous works, we considered the particular cases where the ray meets arbitrarily short closed geodesics or closed horocycles. Here we complete the study by treating the third possible case, where the ray meets closed hypercycles of arbitrarily small length.

papers.title: A five-species counterexample to the Hofbauer--Kon--Saito conjecture on qualitative permanence
papers.abstract: Hofbauer, Kon and Saito (J. Math. Biol. 2008) showed that a Lotka-Volterra interaction matrix $A$ with negative diagonal can be qualitatively permanent only if (C1) every cycle of length $\ge 2$ of $A$ is nonpositive and (C2) every negative cycle contains exactly one negative entry. They conjectured that these conditions are also sufficient, and proved this for $n\le 3$. We give a $5\times 5$ integer matrix with seven nonzero off-diagonal entries that satisfies (C1) and (C2) but is not qualitatively permanent. For an explicit integer growth vector the system has an interior equilibrium, and an asymptotically stable heteroclinic cycle on the boundary of the orthant attracts an open set of interior orbits. Adding non-interacting species gives counterexamples for every $n\ge 5$. The interactions form a one-way feedback loop (two one-sided benefits and one one-sided harm) together with a predator of two prey. The verification is elementary except for one heteroclinic connection, which lies in a face that is not Volterra-Lyapunov stable. For it we prove a connection lemma based on invasion graphs.

papers.title: Early warning of critical transitions: Distinguishing supercritical and subcritical bifurcations from noisy observations
papers.abstract: Early-warning methods can indicate that a system is approaching a loss of stability, but they do not usually reveal whether the approaching bifurcation is supercritical or subcritical. We investigate whether this distinction can be made from noisy pre-transition observations. For this investigation, we extend a regression-based stability method by including the leading cubic nonlinear term, whose sign is used to predict the bifurcation type. We test the method on a stochastic pitchfork model and a spatial stochastic Swift-Hohenberg equation. In both models, classification improves with longer observation horizons, closer proximity to the bifurcation, stronger noise, and larger nonlinear effects. However, these conditions are also linked to a higher risk of noise-induced tipping in the subcritical case. The useful early-warning window is therefore determined by a balance between obtaining enough information to identify the bifurcation type and doing so before noise-induced tipping becomes too likely. In spatially extended systems, we find that observing the full spatial field allows classification over shorter observation horizons, and performance improves when a broader range of spatial modes contributes to the observed dynamics. Altogether, we identify the conditions under which the method can reliably distinguish between supercritical and subcritical bifurcations.

papers.title: Regular closedness off the real axis for root closures of bounded-height integer polynomials
papers.abstract: For each integer $h\ge1$, let $Z_h$ be the closure in the complex plane of the roots of nonzero integer polynomials whose coefficients have absolute value at most $h$, with no degree restriction. We prove that $Z_h$ is regular closed off the real axis: every non-real point of $Z_h$ is a limit of interior points. The root-closure identification of Espigul\'e and Juher, for which we include a self-contained proof, shows that the same closure arises from monic polynomials and that outside the closed unit disc it is the connectedness locus of $h+1$ equally spaced collinear similarities. The main step proves that this locus is regular closed off the real axis; this was known for $h=1$ by Calegari, Koch and Walker, for $h\ge19$, and inside an explicit lens. The symmetry $z\mapsto1/z$ then gives the full-plane statement. The proof adapts the method of traps of Calegari, Koch and Walker, using a neighboring-piece criterion, short chains through consecutive digits, and Rouch\'e's theorem. We also classify the convex attractors.

papers.title: Networks with Memory and Isospectral Reduction
papers.abstract: Restricting the linear dynamics of a graph to selected vertices generally introduces memory, because interactions can pass through hidden vertices before returning. The resulting rational memory kernels give isospectral reduction a dynamical interpretation and identify latent graph symmetries with symmetries of the observed evolution.

papers.title: The inverse problem for Julia limiting directions in the Eremenko--Lyubich class
papers.abstract: We study the inverse problem for Julia limiting directions in the Eremenko-Lyubich class $\mathcal B$, which is the class of transcendental entire functions with a bounded set of singular values, and its meromorphic generalization $\mathcal B_{mer}$. Every nonempty compact subset of the circle can be the set of Julia limiting directions of an entire $f\in\mathcal B$. For finite unions of nondegenerate closed arcs, the corresponding $f\in\mathcal B$, even with every finite order at or above an explicit bound determined by the arc lengths, can be attained. We also refine the series construction of the latter two authors to obtain $f\in \mathcal B_{mer}$ with any prescribed order and the set of Julia limiting directions.

papers.title: Frequency-induced Tipping: Resonance-Driven Tipping in a Threshold Predator-Prey System
papers.abstract: Tipping points refer to abrupt, substantial, and often irreversible transitions in dynamic systems that can be triggered by minor perturbations. Existing tipping mechanisms are usually classified by the nature of the trigger: bifurcation-induced tipping occurs when a parameter crosses a critical threshold, noise-induced tipping is caused by random perturbations, rate-induced tipping occurs when a system fails to track a moving attractor, and phase-induced tipping is triggered by timed perturbations relative to an oscillatory state. In this paper, we identify a new mechanism for tipping: frequency-induced tipping, in which periodic forcing drives a transition through resonant amplification. This occurs by destabilization of an equilibrium via subthreshold perturbations of the appropriate frequency. Filippov analysis of a piecewise-smooth model identifies admissible crossings that lead either to predator loss or to extinction of predator and prey, and numerical simulations show that tipping persists after smoothing of the thresholds. These results extend the current tipping framework to include critical transitions under recurrent environmental forcing.

papers.title: Dynamic invisibility of implicit and nested state-dependent delays in a class of externally forced delay equations
papers.abstract: Delayed feedback is a fundamental mechanism in many systems and is often modeled by delay differential equations (DDEs). While delays are frequently assumed to be constant, in realistic feedback processes they may depend on the state and even be defined implicitly or in a nested fashion by the feedback relation itself. In this work, we address the question of how such implicit and nested state-dependent delays affect the observed behavior of a class of externally forced systems with negative switched feedback. Our motivating example and principal case study is the piecewise-smooth limiting form of a conceptual DDE model for the El Ni\~no-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) with a negative feedback term subject to implicit state-dependent delay. We prove, for a wider prototypical class of DDEs with switched negative feedback and more general forcing, that (subject to an explicit condition on the parameters) any finite level of nested state-dependent delay and the limiting implicit delay are dynamically invisible: they all generate exactly the same trajectory, namely, that of the corresponding constant-delay DDE. We also discuss how the delayed argument functions organize the temporal order of reactions (TOR) in this regime, and show that a more stringent condition is required to ensure TOR for nested state-dependent delays.

papers.title: The entropy spectra of chaotic maps of an interval
papers.abstract: For a continuous self-map f of a real interval L, let ent(f) denote the supremum of the topological entropies of the restrictions of f to its compact invariant sets; for a compact interval this is the usual topological entropy. For a class P of maps, the entropy spectrum of P is the set of values ent(f) taken by the maps f in P. We determine the entropy spectra of the three standard classes of chaotic maps of the compact interval [0,1]. Devaney chaotic maps have spectrum [(1/2) log 2, infinity], maps of positive entropy have spectrum (0, infinity], and Li-Yorke chaotic maps have spectrum [0, infinity]; thus every entropy compatible with the known lower bounds actually occurs, and the three spectra are strictly nested. Mixing maps have spectrum ((1/2) log 2, infinity], and Devaney chaotic maps with at least two fixed points have spectrum [log 2, infinity]. As a consequence, a Devaney chaotic map of the interval attains the minimal entropy (1/2) log 2 only if it has a unique fixed point and is not mixing. For an arbitrary interval, compact or not, maps with a point of least period n have spectrum [log sigma_n, infinity], where sigma_n are the Stefan constants, and Li-Yorke chaotic maps have spectrum [0, infinity]. The proofs combine a truncation theorem for maps of non-compact intervals, showing that clipping a map to a compact subinterval never creates entropy; a horseshoe argument showing that two fixed points force entropy log 2 on transitive maps; and explicit constructions, including an exact piecewise linear family, a mixing map of infinite entropy, and a square-root construction that halves the entropy of a transitive map.

papers.title: A Sharp Bound of Crossing Limit Cycle for Planar piecewise linear Systems with a Straight Switching Line
papers.abstract: Determining the maximum number of crossing limit cycles in planar discontinuous piecewise linear systems separated by a straight line is a central problem in nonsmooth dynamical systems and a natural piecewise-linear counterpart of Hilbert's sixteenth problem, yet its sharp uniform upper bound has long remained an open problem. In this paper, we prove that any such system admits at most three crossing limit cycles. Combined with known examples realizing three crossing limit cycles, this result establishes that three is the sharp uniform upper bound.

papers.title: Solutions to several problems on infinite sumset configurations
papers.abstract: We resolve a number of the problems collected by Kra, Moreira, Richter and Robertson in their survey "Problems on infinite sumset configurations in the integers and beyond". Our main result is that in every countably infinite abelian group, every set of positive upper Banach density contains a sumset $B_1+\dots+B_k$ of $k$ infinite sets, for every $k$; the proof uses the Kronecker factor, but no higher-order Host-Kra structure theory, nilsystems of step greater than one, or nilspaces. We also answer, positively or negatively, questions on monochromatic sets $B+mB$, on sumsets in sets of logarithmic density, on polynomial sumset configurations, on sums of the form $B_{i_1}+\dots+B_{i_m}$ with $B_i$ drawn from a density family, on random sets, on ordered sumsets in shifted primes, on sums and products in $\mathbb{N}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$, and on sumsets in abelian groups. Several of these answers concern the questions as literally stated, and two follow directly from known examples; in each case we say so and discuss the natural corrected question. Finally, answering a question of Kousek and Radi\'c, we show that the supremum of the lower Banach densities of sets $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ such that $B+B+t\not\subset A$ for every infinite $B\subset\mathbb{N}$ and every $t\ge0$ (respectively $B+B\not\subset A$ for every infinite $B$) is $1/2$ (respectively $3/4$). The main theorem and most of the other results are formalized in Lean 4, with some published theorems entering as explicit hypotheses.

papers.title: Slow Entropy of Quasi-Unipotent Actions on S-Arithmetic Homogeneous Spaces
papers.abstract: We study metric and topological slow entropy for translations on a class of finite-volume $S$-arithmetic homogeneous spaces with a real and $p$-adic factor. We consider translations whose real component is quasi-unipotent and whose $p$-adic component lies in a compact open subgroup. At polynomial scales, we show that the metric and topological slow entropies coincide and are determined by the chain structure of the real adjoint action. In particular, the non-Archimedean component contributes no additional polynomial slow entropy. Our result extends the slow entropy formula of Kanigowski, Vinhage, and Wei for quasi-unipotent flows on real homogeneous spaces to this $S$-arithmetic setting.

papers.title: A complete theory of local minimizers for periodic variational problems
papers.abstract: We study the periodic problem in the Calculus of Variations and give a complete characterization of the positive definiteness of the second variation, extending the Reid Roundabout Theorem to periodic boundary conditions. Two formulations are established: one in terms of conjugate and semi-coupled points, and one in terms of the existence of a symmetric solution of the associated Riccati equation satisfying a boundary inequality. We show by an explicit example that the latter condition, while sufficient, is not necessary except in dimension one. As applications, we obtain sufficient conditions for weak and strong local minimizers of periodic solutions of the Euler-Lagrange equation.

papers.title: Cocycles on Tiling Spaces
papers.abstract: The space of tilings by rectangles form an interesting collection of multidimensional subshifts. Here, we study cocycles on such tiling spaces and provide an algorithmically decidable necessary and sufficient condition for the tiling space associated with a collection of rectangles to admit a nontrivial cocycle. Along the way, we also prove that the tiling spaces corresponding to a class of rectangular tile sets satisfy certain mixing properties.

papers.title: On record behaviours of returns for interval maps
papers.abstract: Given a dynamical system $(X,T)$ and an ergodic invariant measure $\mu$, a $\mu$-typical point $x\in X$ under $T$ visits arbitrarily small neighbourhood of $x$. We will use techniques based on extreme value theory and Laplace functional for point process to show that, for interval maps with suitable mixing and anti-clustering conditions, the limiting distributions of the record times and values of the return process $Y_j(x)=-\log d(T^jx,x)$, after possible normalisation, has Poisson-type laws.

papers.title: Dynamical relations on $\mathbb{P}^1$, higher bifurcations, and arithmetic bigness
papers.abstract: In this article, we study algebraic relations among rational maps on $\mathbb{P}^1$ and among their preperiodic points. Working over $\mathbb{C}$, we characterize algebraic families of positive-dimensional varieties in $(\mathbb{P}^1)^N$ and tuples of maps $(f_1, \ldots, f_N)$ for which the subvariety is dynamically special for a Zariski-dense set of parameters. Moreover, outside of well-understood elliptic phenomena, we show that all families of maps and subvarieties that bifurcate are maximally bifurcating. Working over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, we characterize arithmetic and geometric potential bigness for the canonical line bundle associated to families of endomorphisms of $(\mathbb{P}^1)^N$ when restricted to the subvarieties. As consequences, we obtain uniform bounds for the periods and preperiods of relations among non-exceptional maps, and we show uniform bounds on the geometry of preperiodic points satisfying these relations. Over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, our results yield corresponding uniform bounds for points and subvarieties satisfying a height gap.

papers.title: Non-Archimedean Rigidity and the Uniform Dynamical Manin--Mumford for $\left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n$
papers.abstract: We prove a uniform form of the dynamical Manin-Mumford conjecture for split endomorphisms $\Phi = \left(f_1,\ldots,f_n\right): \left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n \to \left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n$ over $\mathbb{C}$, where each $f_i$ has degree $d \geq 2$ and at most one $f_i$ is exceptional. Specifically, we bound the number of irreducible components of $\overline{\operatorname{Prep}\left(\Phi\right)\cap V\left(\mathbb{C}\right)}^{\operatorname{Zar}}$ uniformly, depending only on $\left(n,d,\operatorname{deg} V\right)$. We also obtain uniform statements for the dynamical Bogomolov conjecture. Our approach combines a degeneration argument via ultrafilters with a new non-archimedean rigidity theorem, along with the quantitative dynamical Zhang's inequality by Mavraki and the second author.

papers.title: Ergodic treeable equivalence relations are richly ergodic
papers.abstract: We study the density of ergodic subrelations in the canonical Polish space of subequivalence relations of a probability-measure-preserving countable Borel equivalence relation. Our main result establishes rich ergodicity for ergodic treeable equivalence relations. The proof combines a strongly increasing exhaustion with relative ergodic hyperfinite decomposition. As an application, for every $2\leq r<\infty$, we show that the product of the dyadic odometer action of $\mathbb{Z}$ with the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{F}_r$ has a richly ergodic orbit relation, whereas the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{F}_r$ does not. Thus rich ergodicity of a free ergodic action is not determined by the acting group.

papers.title: On generic subsystems of a Smale space
papers.abstract: We study properties of generic compact invariant subsystems of a fixed Smale space in the Hausdorff topology. For a transitive Smale space, we show that the hyperspace of all subsystems contains an open and dense family of NMC subsystems, a dynamically degenerate class with finite orbit structure. A substantially different picture emerges in the closure of the infinite transitive locus: minimality, unique ergodicity, and zero topological entropy are generic, while subsystems conjugate to regular Toeplitz shifts are dense. Despite generic zero entropy, typical subsystems exhibit large oscillations in complexity: we prove that they have infinite slow entropy at the polynomial scale, and their slow entropy at the stretched-exponential scale is equal to one. For mixing Smale spaces, we further study the closure of the infinite totally transitive subsystems. In this hyperspace, minimality, unique ergodicity, and zero entropy remain generic; the conjugacy class of any Sturmian subshift is dense; and uniquely ergodic subsystems whose invariant measure is weakly mixing form a residual set. In particular, topological weak mixing is generic in this space.

papers.title: Bilinear operators along variable curves
papers.abstract: Motivated by Zygmund's differentiation conjecture and Stein's conjecture for Lipschitz vector fields, we study bilinear singular integral and maximal operators along variable curves given by $$ \begin{aligned} BH_a^\alpha(f,g)(x) &= \operatorname{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb R} f(x-t) g\left(x + a(x)t^\alpha\right)\,\frac{dt}{t},\\ BM_a^\alpha(f,g)(x) &= \sup_{r>0}\frac{1}{2r}\int_{-r}^{r} \left|f(x-t)g\left(x+a(x)t^\alpha\right)\right|\,dt,\\ BSH_c^\alpha(f,g)(x) &= \operatorname{p.v.} \int_{\mathbb R} f(x-t) g(x + t^\alpha)\, \frac{dt}{t-c(x)}, \end{aligned} $$ where $\alpha > 0$ and $a,c:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ are measurable. For every $\alpha>0$ and $0<A<B<\infty$, we construct a smooth, globally Lipschitz coefficient $a:\mathbb R\to(A,B)$ such that, for every H\"{o}lder conjugate pair $1<p,q<\infty$, no strong--type $L^p(\mathbb R)\times L^q(\mathbb R)\to L^1(\mathbb R)$ estimate holds for $BH_a^\alpha$ or $BM_a^\alpha$ on $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)\times C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$; moreover, there exist nonnegative smooth inputs in $\bigcap_{s>1}L^s(\mathbb R)$, one of which is compactly supported, whose outputs under $BH_a^\alpha$ and $BM_a^\alpha$ do not belong to $L^1(\mathbb R)$. For any measurable $a:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $BM_a^\alpha$ maps $L^p(\mathbb R) \times L^q(\mathbb R)$ boundedly into $L^r(\mathbb R)$ whenever $1<p,q\leq\infty$, $1/r = 1/p + 1/q$, and $r > 1$, and maps $L^p(\mathbb R) \times L^q(\mathbb R)$ into weak $L^1(\mathbb R)$ when $1/p+1/q=1$, with constants independent of $a$. Finally, we investigate the shifted operator $BSH_c^\alpha$, including dyadic-integer-valued $c$, and prove that there is a measurable choice of $c$ such that the operator admits no bounded $L^p(\mathbb R) \times L^q(\mathbb R) \to L^{r,\infty}(\mathbb R)$ estimates in the range $1 \leq p,q \leq \infty$ and $\frac{1}{2}<r<\infty$, resolving an open problem posed by Gaitan and Lie.

papers.title: Spontaneous Spirals in Spatial Systems
papers.abstract: Several chemical and biological systems produce spontaneous spirals in their dynamical behavior, such as the Belousov-Zhabotinsky reaction in chemistry and the slime mold Dictyostelium in biology. In a previous study, such spiral wave formation was accurately replicated with a computational spatial system known as the Ideal Storage Cellular Automaton Model (ISCAM). Here, a more detailed investigation is presented of the ability of this model to generate spontaneous spirals depending on its parameter values. A dynamical systems analysis is performed, and bifurcation diagrams, phase space diagrams, and snapshots of the model's spatial dynamics are presented for a range of parameter values. This analysis reveals that spiral waves can only be sustained in the system when the parameter values of the model fall well within the regime of a so-called Neimark-Sacker bifurcation.

papers.title: Large deviations for random walks generated by countable groups: a unified approach
papers.abstract: We present a unified treatment of various large deviation principles in the context of random walks induced by actions of countable groups. The fundamental notion undergirding the global perspective is that of weakly almost additive random walks, inspired by earlier works on the metric geometry of group actions as well as by recent developments in the theory of nonadditive thermodynamic formalism. We treat large deviations of the renormalized vector-valued distance function from the origin for groups acting simultaneously, by isometries and in a weakly almost additive fashion, on an arbitrary number of metric spaces. The foremost class of examples is provided by group actions with contracting elements, which encompasses, among others, actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and mapping class group actions on Teichm\"uller spaces. We further establish large deviation principles for quasimorphisms on countable groups, and for random walks generated by compositions of Euclidean isometries; also, we discuss extensions and streamlining of known large deviation results for singular values of random matrix products. Finally, in all the contemplated cases, we investigate the analytic properties of the rate function, leveraging its expression as the Fenchel-Legendre transform of a pressure function for certain nonadditive sequences of potentials on shift spaces.
